messages:
jen (Jen K.): Quick sync — ran into a confusing case with role inheritance + quota overrides in the console. TL;DR: tenant admin sets RoleA with route:predict permission, then a child scope adds a quota override that effectively blocks predict for some routes. The UI shows RoleA -> predict as granted but the route is still throttled to 0. Users are confused. Should the console show an "effective permissions" view that folds quotas/policies into granted/denied? :thinking:

sachin: Yeah we see this pattern in a few enterprise tenants. The model routing policy can set route-level deny/limit. The trouble is current console only shows role bindings, not derived decisioning. So folks expect the role to be authoritative.

maria: Agree — customers expect one place to see why a route is blocked. Two quick options: 1) Annotate role rows with warnings when a downstream policy overrides, 2) Add an "effective access" panel per-route that queries the same engine we use at runtime.

lee: Option 2 sounds correct but requires an API. We don't currently expose the decision engine as a read API for the console. We'd need something like GET /tenants/:id/effective-permissions?route=... which runs policy evaluation (fast) and returns the decision + provenance.

nate: Implementation note: the runtime uses smart routing + quota matching; evaluation is cheap but must be safe for UI scale. If console polls every route for dozens of tenants, that will spike metrics. We should cache decisions and invalidate on policy/role change.

phil: Also telemetry: we need to emit a permission-eval trace event so admins can see why a production call was allowed/blocked. That event should include matched policies, quotas, and role bindings (redacted principals). Ops-bot can store sampling rate metadata.

ops-bot: suggestion: sample 1% of realtime evals, capture full envelope, and write to perm-evals-sample topic with tenant_id, route, decision, matched_rules.

maria: UX-wise: small MVP = per-route "Why blocked/allowed" flyout that calls the new read API on demand (not poll). Show concise reasons (e.g., "Quota override at scope x sets max_tpm=0") and a link to open the role binding edit modal.

jen (Jen K.): That seems like a good path. Concerns: 1) security — we must ensure the API respects SSO roles (only tenant admins can see decision provenance), 2) performance/cost, 3) rollout plan.

sachin: Security: decision API should require console token scoped to tenant_admin. Also audit log an event when a user views provenance. We already have audit-write infra; just add an audit entry type: permission_provenance_view.

lee: For performance, implement server-side caching keyed by (tenant, route, roleset hash, policy version). Cache TTL short (30s) and invalidate on policy update events. That will make on-demand UI calls cheap and safe.

nate: Rollout: feature-flag gated. Canary to 5 internal tenants, then open to early access. Console changes are front-end only until API exists; we can stub a "reason not available" fallback for customers without backend support.

phil: Telemetry specifics: add a small histogram for permission-eval latency, add a counter for provenance_views (by tenant), and tag events with policy_version. Also create a dashboard panel in Redwood Console Ops showing top "deny reasons" over 24h.

jen (Jen K.): One more complicated bit: quota overrides can be cumulative (route quota + tenant quota + tenant-wide burst bucket). Provenance needs to show ordered evaluation and effective numeric result. UX should surface the final numeric limit and where each number comes from.

maria: Agreed. Example flyout content:
```
Effective decision: DENY (0 tpm)
Sources:
 - route override: max_tpm=0 (scope: service-team-alpha)
 - tenant-wide quota: max_tpm=200
 - role binding: RoleA grants predict
Provenance: route override short-circuited evaluation
```

lee: That example is perfect. Backend should return a small array of provenance steps with stable labels. Keep shape simple so frontend doesn't need complex logic.

sachin: API proposal: GET /v1/tenants/:tid/effective-permissions?route=...&principal=... Response: { decision: "ALLOW|DENY", reason_summary: string, steps: [{type, source_id, detail}], policy_version: string } — but of course we'll version it and return JSON.

phil: Minor ask: include an options param ?include_references=true to return policy ids that can be linked to console edit pages (subject to auth).

jen (Jen K.): Ok next: what about telemetry cost? If we sample eval traces at 1% by default but the provenance_view API also writes an audit entry, that's extra events. We should batch audit writes and avoid capturing full token payload.

nate: Batch not necessary for audit (small). But for perm-evals-sample topic, ensure we scrub user content and API keys. Use redact policy.

maria: UX decision for display: show both "granted by role X" and "overridden by policy Y" with clear visual weight to final decision. Avoid overloading non-admins — only show provenance to tenant admins and service owners.

jen (Jen K.): Action items:
- lee: spike API + cache (owner) — estimate 3d to make a proto endpoint that reads from policy engine (no auth) and 1w to make production with auth + cache.
- phil: add telemetry counters/histograms and dashboard panel (owner) — 2d for initial metrics + dash stub.
- maria: mockups for flyout + warning badges in role grid — 1d.
- sachin: audit + sampling rules + redact plan (owner) — 2d.

phil: I'll own rollout doc and feature flag gating. We'll also add a CLI flag for operators to disable provenance sampling at tenant level.

jen (Jen K.): Great. Quick follow-ups: lee post the API spec here when you have the proto. Also include a sample curl. If anyone has objections to the approach speak now, otherwise we'll kick off and sync in tomorrow eng sync. :+1:

lee: Will do. Proto posted in ~24h. No objections from me.

sachin: No objections. Small note: for multi-region tenants, ensure evaluation uses policy_version replicated across regions to avoid inconsistent results.

jen (Jen K.): Good catch — add that to spike.

console-bot: deploy scheduled: permission-provenance-proto branch -> staging at 2024-11-02T03:00:00Z (testing only).

phil: Thanks all. Closing thread for now. We'll track progress in the PR description. :)
